transcript: Three meals a day is the biggest lie they ever sold us. Here's why. Most people don't eat because they're hungry anymore. They eat because the clock tells them to eat. Morning comes, they say breakfast. Noon comes, they say lunch. Night comes, they say dinner. And in between, they snack because they're bored, stressed, tired, or because the body is confused from eating all day. But listen carefully. Your stomach was never meant to work nonstop from the moment you wake up until the moment you sleep. When you keep putting food inside the body all day, the body has no time to rest, no time to clean, and no time to reset. This is why so many people feel bloated, heavy, tired after eating, and still somehow hungry again one hour later. The problem is not always that you need more food. Sometimes your body needs better digestion. Sometimes your body needs water. Sometimes your body needs fiber because fiber helps you feel fuller, supports your gut, and helps things move the way they should. In the old days, people didn't count every meal. They ate real food. They ate slowly, and they stopped before the body became heavy. Today, people eat fast, eat processed food, and then wonder why the stomach feels like a stone. So before your next meal, ask yourself one question. Am I truly hungry, or am I just following a habit they taught me? Because the man who cannot control his appetite will always be controlled by someone else. If your digestion feels slow, bloated, or heavy, I put the fiber I personally recommend in the link on my profile. Comment, fiber, and follow for more old monk health lessons.
